title: Upgrade to v1.26.0 (IAVL fast-node read-path correctness — coordinated activation of patches/iavl fix)
summary: Coordinated activation of a state-machine-breaking fix to blockchain/patches/iavl. The deployed IAVL patch treated a fast-node index miss at the latest version as proof of key absence — instead of falling back to the canonical IAVL tree. That is the root cause of the post-state-sync `mint.BondDenom == ""` panic that took down mirage.talk on 2026-05-25 after watchdog recovery, and is the evidence-consistent cause of the original block 4,854,225 app-hash divergence on the same node (the same IAVL read contract was on the deliver path; not formally reproduced because we lack per-node IAVL state captures from that moment). After v1.26.0, every IAVL read path — ImmutableTree.Get, MutableTree.GetVersioned, ImmutableTree.Iterator, ImmutableTree.Iterate, MutableTree.Iterator, MutableTree.Iterate — falls through to canonical IAVL on a fast-node miss. Fast-node hits are still served from the index for performance. The handler is a no-op for on-chain state (no new params, no new store keys, no module migrations) — coordination is required because pre- and post-v1.26.0 nodes will compute different app hashes from the same canonical state if one of them hits a fast-node miss. After this upgrade is live across the validator set, state-sync recovery is safe again on this chain.
